en: Points of Controversy Great Section Twelfth Chapter
The Discourse on Taking Life:
"Does a person endowed with right view intentionally deprive a living being of life?
"Yes."
A person endowed with right view might intentionally deprive his mother of life...
[and so on] ...deprive his father of life...
[and so on] ...deprive an arahant of life... [and so on].
"Could one, with a malicious mind, draw blood from a Tathāgata...
or cause a schism in the Saṅgha?
"One must not say so... [and so on].
"Does a person endowed with right view intentionally deprive a living being of life?
"Yes.
"Is such a person lacking in reverence toward the Teacher?"
It should not be said thus … [and so on for] the Dhamma … the Saṅgha … [and so on].
"Is one who lacks reverence for the training so described? "One should not say so. ... [etc. ...
"But is not a person endowed with right view one who has reverence for the Teacher?"
“Yes.
“If a person possessed of right view has reverence for the Teacher, then surely it should not be said:
‘A person possessed of right view might intentionally deprive a living being of life.’”
Is it not the case that a person endowed with right view has reverence for the Dhamma … [and so on] … for the Saṅgha … [and so on] … for the training?
“Yes.
“If a person endowed with right view has reverence for the training, then surely it should not be said:
‘A person endowed with right view might intentionally deprive a living being of life.’”
Is a person possessed of right view disrespectful toward the Teacher? Yes.
Would such a person defile a stupa of the Buddha, pollute it, spit upon it, or treat the stupa of the Buddha with contempt?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Would a person endowed with right view intentionally deprive a living being of life?
Yes.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
"Just as, monks, the great ocean is stable in its nature and does not overstep its shore,
even so, monks, whatever training rule has been laid down by me for my disciples, that my disciples do not transgress even for the sake of their lives"?
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“Could a person endowed with right view intentionally deprive a living being of life?
The discussion on the taking of life is concluded.
